subject: Urgent: BarnesHealth production throttling — quota/burst policy mismatch
messages:
From: Sam Barnes <sam.barnes@barneshealth.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Apr 2029 15:12:03 -0700
Subject: High 5xx/latency during morning peak - causing user impact

Vanessa / Monica,

We started seeing elevated latency and a burst of 5xx errors around 08:15 PDT this morning during our batch ingest window. Error rate jumped to ~18% for ~10 minutes and our customers reported timeouts. Attached are a few example request IDs and timestamps.

Request sample: 2029-04-26T15:14:22Z id=bh-req-7f4c
Error: 429 / 503 with message "rate limit exceeded" and increased p95 latency from 180ms -> 1.2s.

This is causing a queue backlog in our downstream processing. Can you confirm whether this is a Redwood-side throttling issue or something on our end? We need immediate mitigation and an explanation for our ops/engineering teams.

Thanks,
Sam
Ops Lead, BarnesHealth
[Attachment: request-sample-logs.txt (text/plain)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Apr 2029 15:43:10 -0700
Subject: Initial triage — spike aligns with policy rollout

Folks — initial triage findings: the spike 15:14–15:24 PDT correlates with the automatic rollout of a revised rate/ burst policy we deployed to the region at 15:12 PDT (partial rollback window). The rollout targeted new tenancy tagging but looks like the selector matched BarnesHealth incorrectly and applied a lower burst allowance.

What I see: increased 429s from our edge -> origin in the same minute buckets; token bucket drain faster than expected. Attached minimal diffs between previous policy and current (policy-diff.txt). I also created RED-3456 for tracking.

Excerpt from edge logs (customer-supplied request id shown):
> 2029-04-26T15:14:22Z edge id=eh-22a, client=bh-org-112, status=429, reason="burst_limit_exceeded"

Temporary mitigation options:
1) Apply a targeted policy override for bh-org-112 to restore previous burst window (fastest, low risk).
2) Roll back the rollout globally (impactful to other customers).
3) Throttle gracefully with queued backoff (will still hit user latency).

I'll prepare a short exec summary for Vanessa if we need sign-off for credits/SLAs.

[Attachment: policy-diff.txt (text/plain)]
[Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-3456]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Apr 2029 16:10:05 -0700
Subject: Root cause — selector mis-evaluated legacy tenancy tag

Short technical summary:
- Root cause: the rollout introduced a selector expression change (tenant_tag in_set ["platinum","premium"]) to target new accounts. BarnesHealth has a legacy tag "enterprise-old" which is not in_set(). Due to a bug in the selector evaluation (missing fallback) the policy engine interpreted the missing tag as a default group with the new lower burst window.
- Effect: burst window reduced from 1,000 tokens/60s -> 200 tokens/60s for bh-org-112; steady-state QPS fine but bursty batch loads overwhelmed the bucket, producing 429/503 cascades and elevated p95.
- Evidence: policy snapshot attached (quota-snapshot-2029-04-26.json) and diff file.

Recommended immediate action (ordered):
1) Apply targeted policy override to restore previous burst window for bh-org-112 (5 min change).
2) Add a temporary emergency rule to exempt legacy tags until selector logic is fixed.
3) Postmortem + config test coverage for selector fallback.

I'll prepare the override playbook and a small config patch; can apply once Vanessa/Marissa approve.

Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
[Attachment: quota-snapshot-2029-04-26.json (application/json)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 26 Apr 2029 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Exec ask: approval for targeted override + customer credit (BarnesHealth) — incident summary

Marissa / Lauren — brief summary and ask: 
- Incident: BarnesHealth experienced a burst of 429/503 and elevated latency during 15:14–15:24 PDT due to a policy selector rollback bug that assigned a lower burst window to their org.
- Impact: ~10 minutes of degraded throughput; customer batch queueing and visible customer complaints to their ops team. No data loss.
- Root cause: selector logic change in rollout matched legacy-tagged orgs to a lower-burst policy (see Jordan/Karthik notes).

Requested approvals: 
1) Approve targeted override now (Jordan/Karthik to apply) to restore previous behavior — immediate mitigation.
2) Approve a customer credit: proposed 25% credit for the billing cycle and written apology + technical summary.
3) Approve a 1-week accelerated patch schedule to add selector fallback tests and a postmortem share-out.

If OK, I'll apply the comms template and Monica will coordinate the customer-facing message. Need decision in the next 20 minutes so we can act before any potential follow-up incidents.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: incident-timeline.pdf (application/pdf)]
